newsitem.title: JAPAN: HANDBALL-SPAIN DEFEAT CROATIA DESPITE ROYAL SUSPENSION.
newsitem.headline: HANDBALL-SPAIN DEFEAT CROATIA DESPITE ROYAL SUSPENSION.

text.p: Despite a two minute suspension of their future prince, Spain beat Olympic champions Croatia 31-25 on Tuesday to reach the quarter-finals of the men's handball world championship.
In other key matches, world champions France scored in the last second to beat hosts Japan 22-21 and Russia overcame Tunisia 20-14, maintaining their undefeated record in the tournament.

Spain's future prince Inaki Urdangarin, penalised twice in the second half for rough play, returned to the court in time to celebrate Spain's victory, payback for Atlanta where Spain were bronze medallists.
Urdangarin, 29, a professional rated among Spain's all-time top five handball players, was engaged last month to Princess Cristina, 31, daughter of King Juan Carlos and Queen Sofia.
Spain had a 16-14 halftime lead, but coach Roman Seco castigated the team at the break for poor passing.
"I instructed the team to calm down and concentrate on accurate passing," Seco said.
Mateo Garralda Larumbe was Spain's top scorer with seven goals followed by former Russian player Talant Dujshebaev and Urdiales Marquez with six goals each.
South Korea scored a 37-33 extra time win over Yugoslavia, a team they had never beaten. The South Koreans beat France in last week's preliminary round.
Yugoslavia were one goal ahead with just 30 seconds of full time left when Kim Yong-jin netted his only goal of the game to tie the match 30-30, sending it into extra time.
France just clinched their success over Japan, scoring the winning goal in the last second.
Russia, the only team to win all five of their preliminary round matches, cruised to victory over Tunisia, establishing themselves as tournament favourites.
Iceland claimed a 32-28 victory over Norway, while Egypt hung on to beat Cuba 24-20.
The quarter-finals will be played on Thursday with the final on Sunday.
